q-957.name: Question 1
q-957.worked_solution:
We use the change of base formula:

$$
{log}_{a}⁡X=\frac{{log}_{b}⁡X}{{log}_{b}⁡a}
$$

In our case, $a=9,$ and $X=27.$ Since both $a$ and $X$ are powers of $3,$ we set $b=3.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{9}⁡(27) & =\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(27)}{{log}_{3}⁡(9)} \\  & =\frac{{log}_{3}⁡({3}^{3})}{{log}_{3}⁡({3}^{2})} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Calculate log9⁡(27) without using a calculator.

a
32
b
34
c
23
d
12
e
13
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We use the change of base formula: loga⁡X=logb⁡Xlogb⁡a

In our case, a=9, and X=27. Since both a and X are powers of 3, we set b=3. So, we have:

log9⁡(27)=log3⁡(27)log3⁡(9)=log3⁡(33)log3⁡(32)=32

q-100672.name: Question 2
q-100672.problem: Use a calculator to evaluate ${log}_{7}⁡(12)$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.
q-100672.worked_solution:
Let's calculate ${log}_{7}⁡(12)$ by changing the base $7$ to the common logarithm (base $10$).

We use the change of base formula:

$$
{log}_{a}⁡X=\frac{{log}_{b}⁡X}{{log}_{b}⁡a}
$$

In our case, $a=7,$ $X=12,$ $b=10.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{7}⁡(12) & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡(12)}{{log}_{10}⁡(7)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(12)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(7)} \\  & ≈\frac{1.079\,18}{0.845\,10} \\  & ≈1.28\end{aligned}
$$
